newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle closes lower, feeders also decline.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle closes lower, feeders also decline.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed slightly lower as the market continued its modest technical downside retracement after last week's run-up to contract highs, dealers said.
"It is just a technical correction," one dealer said.

Floor sources said the main sellers in August were rolling forward long positions into October while Cargill Investor Services was a noted buyer. Refco and R.J. O'Brien were featured sellers of October with locals on the buy side.
August closed off 0.275 cent lower at 65.775 cents with other months 0.625 to 0.200 cent down.
Dealers noted August had been overbought after setting a contract high of 66.900 cents last week following a rapid rise of about four cents in a week.
The market's upward momentum was also hurt by Friday's USDA cattle-on-feed report which showed that a lower than expected number of cattle had been marketed during June.
There also continued to be concern that cattle were being marketed at heavier weights.
Feeders also closed lower, weakened by a modest advance in CBOT corn prices and indications the market was overbought. August feeders closed 0.675 cent lower at 82.075 cents.
Other months were down 1.050 to 0.675 cents.
Floor sources said Refco were a featured seller of August feeders and a noted buyer of October. R.J. O'Brien were the major seller of October.
The latest CME feeder index, for July 21, was off $0.10 at $82.04 per cwt.
